learningObjective: Contrast fully shape-specialized compilation with dynamic-shape compilation and identify the trade-offs each incurs.

canonicalClaims.claim: Shape specialization enables tile-size and constant-dependent optimizations that dynamic-shape emitters cannot exploit, but pays a compile-time and artifact-storage cost proportional to the number of specialized shapes; dynamic-shape emitters amortize one artifact over a shape range at some per-shape performance cost.
conditions: The compiler supports both modes and can bucket if desired.
The workload's shape distribution is characterized (single hot shape vs. many rare shapes).
nonImplications: Does not imply one mode is universally superior; hybrid bucket-and-specialize strategies exist.
Does not imply dynamic shapes affect correctness — they are semantics-preserving.

misconceptions.claim: Full shape specialization is strictly faster at runtime than dynamic-shape compilation for any workload.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Rare / single-use shapes make specialization a net loss when compile time is included in the latency budget.

misconceptions.claim: Dynamic-shape compilation produces incorrect results for shape-dependent numerics like broadcasts.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dynamic-shape compilation tracks broadcasts symbolically and preserves semantics; correctness does not depend on compile-time shape knowledge.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: TorchInductor / TVM Relax symbolic shape docs

misconceptions.claim: Bucketing shapes into a small number of specialized artifacts is impossible because every bucket boundary must be a compile-time constant.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Bucket boundaries are chosen at compile time; runtime shapes are dispatched to the nearest bucket-specialized artifact.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: Production LLM serving stacks (vLLM prefill length bucketing)

misconceptions.claim: Dynamic-shape compilation emits one kernel that handles all shapes at zero runtime cost.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dynamic-shape kernels typically pay for runtime tail handling, guard checks, and slightly less aggressive tile-size choices.

implementationFacts: TorchInductor's `dynamic=True` mode uses symbolic integer sizes and inserts runtime guards.
TVM Relax supports symbolic tensor shapes with runtime dispatch.
Production LLM systems commonly bucket batch and sequence lengths into a small set of specialized kernels.
performanceScenarios: A single hot shape sees specialization win by 5-20%; a broad shape distribution sees dynamic-shape or bucketing win overall due to amortized compile cost.
